chapters.summary: Council staff greets attendees and calls the Committee on Public Safety vote to order. Staff asks everyone to silence electronics and refrain from approaching the dais, then invites the chair to begin.
chapters.title: Staff opens Public Safety Committee vote and sets room procedures

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning, good morning.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Welcome to the New York City Council Committee Vote on Public Safety.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At this time, we ask that you please silence all electronics.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: And please do not approach the dais.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair, you may begin.

chapters.summary: Chair Oswald J. Feliz greets everyone and identifies himself as chair of the Committee on Public Safety. He recognizes committee members Hanks, Justin Sanchez, Gutierrez, Hankerson, Vernikov, Wong, and Banks.
chapters.title: Chair Feliz calls meeting to order and introduces committee members

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: My name is Oswald Feliz, and I am the chair of the Committee on Public Safety.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I would like to recognize members of the committee, including council members Hanks, Justin Sanchez, Gutierrez, Hankerson, Council Member Vernikov, Wong, and Banks.

chapters.summary: Chair Feliz states that the committee will vote on Proposed Introduction 489-A, sponsored by Council Member Inna Vernikov. He identifies the bill as the item of business before the committee.
chapters.title: Chair Feliz announces vote on Intro 489-A sponsored by Vernikov

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Today, the committee will vote on proposed introduction number 489A, sponsored by Councilmember Ina Vernikov.

chapters.summary: Chair Feliz says the bill would require the city to create and maintain a centralized online database for vehicles towed from public or private property by city or licensed private tow operators. He explains it would replace confusing existing procedures where owners search competing databases or call local police precincts.
chapters.title: Chair Feliz explains centralized towed-vehicle database replacing old procedures

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: This bill will require the city to create and maintain a centralized online database that allows a member of the public to search for information related to vehicles that have been towed from public or private property by the city or licensed private tow operator.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: This centralized database will replace existing procedures that often frustrate vehicle owners, where individuals must search competing toll databases or contact the local police precinct to locate vehicles towed within the city.

chapters.summary: Chair Feliz outlines the database's opt-in notification system that would alert vehicle owners when their vehicle information is entered into the towing database. He urges colleagues to support the common-sense legislation and invites Council Member Ina Vernikov to say a few words on her bill.
chapters.title: Chair Feliz describes opt-in notifications and invites Vernikov to speak

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Additionally, the centralized database will have functionality to allow vehicle owners to opt in to a notification system that allows vehicle owners

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: if their vehicle information is entered into the towing database.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I urge my colleagues to support this common sense piece of legislation that will improve the city's delivery of services and simplify the process for drivers to locate towed vehicles.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Before turning to the clerk to conduct the vote, I'd like to invite Councilmember Ina Bernikoff to say a few words on her bill.

chapters.summary: Council Member Inna Vernikov thanks Chair Feliz and Public Safety Committee members for their patience and support. She says the bill is the result of bipartisan cooperation, many meetings, and work with agencies and towing businesses.
chapters.title: Vernikov thanks committee and credits bipartisan work on towed-vehicle bill

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: Thank you, everyone, for being so patient.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Feliz, members of the Public Safety Committee.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: I am thrilled that this bill is up for a vote today.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: This bill is the result of a lot of bipartisan cooperation, many, many meetings, work of many agencies, towing businesses, and a lot of drafts.

chapters.summary: Vernikov explains that Intro 489-A would create one centralized online database allowing the public to search for any vehicle moved or towed by a city entity or licensed private tow operator. She says it replaces an old, non-functional system that forced owners to search multiple databases or call precincts.
chapters.title: Vernikov details centralized database to locate towed vehicles

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: Introduction 489A will create a centralized database, online database, that allows the public to search for information on any vehicle

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: that has been moved or towed from public or private property by a city entity or licensed private tow operator.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: This will replace a very old, non-functional system and procedures that have frustrated many vehicle owners, where before they'd be searching through many different old databases with little success or calling police precincts.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: New Yorkers will be able to go on to one centralized portal to locate their towed vehicle, which will greatly limit frustration and save them time, hassle, and perhaps some money for the most difficult cases.

chapters.summary: Vernikov describes the database's optional notification function that would alert vehicle owners if their vehicle was moved or towed. She says this will save New Yorkers time, hassle, and money in difficult cases.
chapters.title: Vernikov highlights opt-in notification feature for towed vehicles

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: Additionally, the database will have a function to allow vehicle owners to opt in to notifications that alerts them if their vehicle was moved or towed.

chapters.summary: Vernikov thanks Speaker Menon, Chair Feliz, Public Safety Committee members, NYPD, DCWP, Department of Finance, and other agencies involved. She also credits Senior Legislative Attorney Josh Kingsley, Peter Spencer, Troy Olson, and members of the public and towing industry who provided input.
chapters.title: Vernikov thanks Speaker, agencies, staff, and towing industry for input

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: I'd like to thank all those who over the past couple of years have helped to see this bill through, Speaker Menon,

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: Chair Feliz, members of the Public Safety Committee, NYPD, DCWP, Department of Finance, and the many different agencies involved in helping to work out the details,

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: including Senior Legislative Attorney for New York City Council Josh Kingsley, Executive Director of the Minority Delegation Peter Spencer, my Legislative Director Troy Olson, as well as members of the public and towing industry who came to me with their input

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: that helped inform the version you'll be voting on today.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: Thank you very much, and I look forward to the public having the convenience of utilizing this great tool.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Chair Feliz thanks Council Member Vernikov for her remarks. He then turns the meeting over to the committee clerk to conduct the vote.
chapters.title: Chair Feliz thanks Vernikov and turns to clerk for roll call

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Councilmember Vernikov.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I'll now turn it to the clerk for a vote.

chapters.summary: Committee Clerk William Martin greets the committee and announces a roll-call vote on Proposed Introduction 489-A. He begins calling members by name.
chapters.title: Clerk William Martin opens roll call on Intro 489-A

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: William Martin, Committee Clerk, Roll Call Vote Committee on Public Safety.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Proposed Introduction 489A.

chapters.summary: The clerk calls Chair Feliz, Gutierrez, Hanks, and Nurse; Feliz, Gutierrez, and Hanks vote aye. Banks is then called and votes aye while congratulating the bill's sponsor.
chapters.title: Roll call begins: Feliz, Gutierrez, Hanks, Banks vote aye

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair Felice.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Aye.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Gutierrez.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Aye.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Hanks.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Aye.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Nurses.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Banks.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Aye, and congratulations on your bill.

chapters.summary: As the clerk reaches Hankerson in the roll call, Chair Feliz interrupts to say he loves Vernikov's bill and needed it two years ago. He thanks her for working on the legislation.
chapters.title: Chair Feliz interjects praise for Vernikov's bill during roll call

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Hankerson.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I just want to say to Councilman Vernikov, I love this bill.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I needed it two years ago, so thank you.

chapters.summary: The clerk resumes the roll call and calls Justin Sanchez and Wong, who vote aye. Ariola is also called before the clerk announces the tally.
chapters.title: Roll call resumes: Sanchez, Wong, Ariola vote aye

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Justin Sanchez.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Aye.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Wong.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: I will aye.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Ariola.

chapters.summary: The clerk reports a vote of seven in the affirmative, zero in the negative, and no abstentions. He declares that Intro 489-A has been adopted by the Committee on Public Safety.
chapters.title: Committee adopts Intro 489-A with seven affirmative votes

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: With a vote of seven in the affirmative, zero in the negative, and no abstentions, item has been adopted by the committee.

chapters.summary: Chair Feliz thanks everyone and congratulates Council Member Vernikov on the bill's adoption. He recounts waking up about a year ago to find his car had disappeared and says he had no idea where it went, so he appreciates the legislation.
chapters.title: Chair Feliz congratulates Vernikov and shares personal towing story

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I want to congratulate Councilmember Vernikov.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I could have used this bill.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: It could have been helpful to me.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: About a year ago, I woke up, went to my car, and learned that my car had literally disappeared.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I had no idea where it went.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: So congratulations.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Thank you for working on this.

chapters.summary: Chair Feliz says he will hold the vote open for a few minutes. Staff notes that a few council members will join.
chapters.title: Chair Feliz holds vote open for additional members

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: We'll hold the vote open for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: A few council members will join.

chapters.summary: After the pause, Chair Feliz thanks everyone and says the bill passes unanimously. He declares the vote closed.
chapters.title: Chair Feliz closes vote and announces Intro 489-A passed unanimously

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Thank you so much, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: The bill passes unanimously.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: The vote is now closed.

summary: The Committee on Public Safety met to vote on Proposed Introduction 489-A, a bill sponsored by Council Member Inna Vernikov to create a centralized online database and opt-in notification system for towed vehicles.
Chair Oswald J. Feliz and members discussed the bill's replacement of fragmented tow-truck lookup procedures and thanked agency and industry stakeholders for their input.
The committee adopted Intro 489-A by a 7-0 roll-call vote, then held the vote open before closing it and confirming unanimous passage.
title: Committee on Public Safety
topic: Requiring the creation of a centralized online database and notification system for towed vehicles, and to repeal section 20-528 of such code, relating to notification of a towed vehicle to a local police precinct
